description: This bar chart, titled "Data sources," illustrates the number of datasets collected each year from 2012 to 2022, categorized by the number of data sources they utilized, as indicated by the legend: blue bars represent datasets using one data source ("1"), and orange bars represent datasets using two or more data sources ("2+"). The horizontal axis, labeled "Year," lists the years sequentially from 2012 to 2022. The vertical axis, labeled "Number of datasets," is scaled linearly from 0 to 100, with tick marks at intervals of 20. For each year, a pair of bars is displayed side-by-side, with the blue bar for "1" source and the orange bar for "2+" sources. The values for the bars are as follows: in 2012, the blue bar is approximately 1 and the orange bar is approximately 1; in 2013, blue is approximately 1 and orange is approximately 1; in 2014, blue is approximately 1 and orange is approximately 1; in 2015, blue is approximately 1 and orange is approximately 1; in 2016, blue is approximately 10 and orange is approximately 2; in 2017, blue is approximately 20 and orange is approximately 5; in 2018, blue is approximately 30 and orange is approximately 18; in 2019, blue is approximately 45 and orange is approximately 18; in 2020, blue is approximately 85 and orange is approximately 43; in 2021, blue is approximately 110 and orange is approximately 45; and in 2022, blue is approximately 30 and orange is approximately 5. Notably, the bars for 2022 are grayed out, indicating they may represent a different category or status compared to the other years. The bars are not sorted and are presented chronologically along the x-axis.
